title: MAME 0.2
subtitle: Nicola Salmoria, 1997 · seven drivers instead of four — 9,215 lines of C89
argsHint: a driver name (pacman, mspacman, puckman, pengo, penta, crush, ladybug, mrdo, cclimber, ckong) plus msdos.c's own switches: -nosound -nojoy -vesa -noscanlines. Leave -nosound OFF to hear it: the SEAL mixer is wired to the page's audio ring.
fpsNote: A FALLBACK cap only. The program paces itself from drv->frames_per_second through the real clock; this bounds a program that does not throttle itself at all.

needsData.hint: each driver's own ROMs, in a directory named after it (pacman/, mrdo/, ...)

safepointsNote: MAME waits for a key to be RELEASED with `while (osd_key_pressed(k));`, and osd_key_pressed is now the game's own C reading Allegro's key[] out of memory -- no call, so nothing outside can see the loop or break it. The safepoint is where key[] gets refreshed, which is also what a real Allegro does from a keyboard interrupt.
